chunks: That is so for God is the Reality, and what they invoke other than Him is illusion. Indeed God is all-high and supreme.
ai.seo_question: Why are false deities considered illusion compared to God in Surah Luqman?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to establish the ontological reality of Tawhid, contrasting the absolute truth of Allah with the contingent, illusory nature of false deities. It underscores the attribute of Al-Ali Al-Kabir, affirming God's transcendence and sovereignty, which serves as the foundation for Luqman's advice to his son to avoid shirk. This distinction between Haqq and Batil is central to understanding the spiritual clarity required for true monotheism.
